note: Reference: the cloth robe's menu, raised on both apps by the same bridge command with the robe in the pack. The five header leaves are quoted RELATIVE to each app's own popup top line (see `anchor`), because they are about the header's CONTENT -- with absolute rects they also silently scored the popup's PLACEMENT, and Raves' popup sits a constant 16px lower, which made a pixel-accurate header read as broken. That offset is now its own leaf, popup_placement.

A composite mean folds a 1px translation and a rasteriser difference into one number; this leaf separates them, which is the spec format's entire argument.

controls_note: fixture_dependent says whether a leaf changes when a DIFFERENT item's popup is scored. It is recorded per leaf because the distinction was already got wrong once on the Equipment spec, where list_cat/list_item were treated as chrome and are not. Only the two leaves with fixture_dependent=false -- popup_image_frame and popup_placement -- are safe as CONTROLS when validating a retaken baseline; everything else moves with the item and would mask a real regression. That is a thin control set, which is exactly why the pin must name the item.

qud_model.measured: 2026-08-08, from Qud's LIVE RectTransforms via the mod's `uiprobe` (target=PopupMessage), on SIX popups across four kinds -- three item menus (7/8/9 options, widths 239.81/278.21/433.61), the wish AskString (650x76.72, no context block), a message notice (462.81x57.12) and the quit confirm (453.40x57.12). Every number below is Qud's own; none is fitted to a capture.
qud_model.root: PopupMessage 1920x1080, VerticalLayoutGroup, align=MiddleCenter, no padding -- Qud CENTRES the popup, it does not place it at a fixed y
qud_model.popup_box: MenuControll x=820.9 y=336.44 w=278.21 h=407.12, VerticalLayoutGroup spacing=10 pad L20 R20 T0 B5, UpperLeft. y is exactly (1080-407.12)/2
qud_model.header_block: ContextContainer h=138.12, VerticalLayoutGroup spacing=10 pad T10, MiddleCenter
qud_model.name_line: ContextItemText x=840.9 y=428.44 w=238.21 h=20.12 -- full content width, so the name is centred on x=960.0, exactly screen centre
qud_model.divider: 'polat frame reverse header' h=16 at y=458.56
qud_model.command_area: Scroll View = Content: pad L5 R5, spacing 2, children Message + options area + inputbox. CONTENT-DEPENDENT and reproduced as such, not matched to one capture: options area = 26 per row with spacing 2, so the 8-option menu's Content is 0 + 2 + 222 = 224 and the 9-option one's is 252. An ABSENT inputbox takes its spacing with it (menu: 0+2+222); an EMPTY options area does not (wish: 20.12 + 2 + 0 + 2 + 17.60 = 41.72).
qud_model.header_block_arithmetic: VERIFIED to the pixel against the probe's own numbers: ContextContainer = padT(10) + tile(72) + spacing(10) + nameLine(20.12) + spacing(10) + divider(16) = 138.12, and the probe reports h=138.12. MenuControll's y is likewise exactly (1080-407.12)/2 = 336.44. So the vertical model is fully derived, not fitted.
qud_model.chrome_vs_box: PORTED 2026-08-08. Qud's visible rules do not bound the centred box: the top rule sits 16 ABOVE MenuControll's top, the opaque fill spans box_top-20 .. box_bottom-2, and the bottom rule sits 15.5 INSIDE the bottom. Pinned to the pixel by two popups whose box origins have different fractional parts (336.44 and 501.64) and whose rules still land on rows 320/486 and 728/563. Raves used to draw its top rule 8px INSIDE the panel and centre the PANEL; it now centres Qud's box and hangs the chrome off it.
qud_model.width_rule: box = 40 + max(context name, 10 + widest row, command bar). Each of the three terms is the one that wins on some popup, which is why one capture could not have taught it: the cloth robe is sized by its widest command (67 + 211.21 = 278.21), the DATA DISK by its 41-character NAME (40 + 393.6 = 433.61, against a command area that only asks for 199.81), and the QUIT CONFIRM by its command bar (3 entries 393.40 + 2 spacings + 2 line sprites at their 25px floor = 453.40, against a message that only asks for 383.40).
qud_model.menu_crome: MenuCrome: 20 tall, spacing 5, MiddleCenter, pad L-20 R-20 so it spans the WHOLE box. Each entry is padL 2 + an 8px Selection Cursor cell (present even unselected) + spacing 5 + text + padR 20 -- the item popup's single '[Esc] Cancel' measures 150.20 against a 115.20 label. The two line sprites take the rest, with a minimum of 25 each; the bottom rule is their ink, at box_bottom - 15.5, with a 1px end tick down each sprite's full 15px height.

offsets_note:
RESOLVED 2026-08-08 by porting the box model whole (godot/PopupOverlay.gd). popup_placement 6.75 -> 0.00 and popup_frame_text_geometry 0.75 -> 0.25; nothing was nudged.

The '16px low' decomposed exactly as recorded: a content-dependent height error plus an anchoring error that happened to sum to 16 on this one menu. Both are gone because the box is now Qud's, not because either was compensated.

THE 1px NAME SHIFT WAS DOWNSTREAM OF THE WIDTH, as predicted here on 2026-08-08 -- it resolved with no change to the name's own layout. What actually caused it: Godot's `get_string_size` returns a WHOLE number where Qud lays this text out at exactly 0.6em (9.6px at font 16), and summing the per-run pieces of a coloured string rounds again. The widest option row measured 213 against Qud's 211.21, the box came out 280 instead of 278.21, and its centred left edge moved a pixel and took the top rule, the divider and the item name with it. Measuring on the font's own pitch instead put the name's ink box at Qud's x, y AND width; the residual 0.25 is 1px of ink HEIGHT, i.e. the rasteriser.

One concession, documented rather than silent: Godot snaps every Control rect to a whole pixel, so the carrier PanelContainer cannot be 278.21 wide. Left alone a Container CEILS a fractional minimum (228.2 -> 229); the model's own widths are rounded to the NEAREST pixel instead, and the chrome is drawn on the exact fractional box rather than on the carrier. That is what makes the AskString's rules land on Qud's rows despite a 76.72 box in a 77px carrier.
